title: Brasswell Mutual - claims LLM onramp scratchbook
body:
One-line: working notes from kickoff + technical capture for Brasswell Mutual claims assistant POC.

Attendees (11/03/2025): Ava M (Redwood CS lead), Liam O'C (Solutions Eng), Priya D (Brasswell PM), Samir P (Brasswell infra), Marcus Leung (Head of Claims ops).

Context / goal: Brasswell wants a fast prototype to triage incoming claims (auto-classify, extract policy ids, surface suggested actions for adjusters). They want something that can be demoed internally in 3 weeks and run as a private deployment (VPC) due to PII/PCI concerns. Long-term: productize with Dedicated capacity and audit logs, possible multi-region DR.

High-level constraints / SLOs they care about:
- P95 latency target for generation path: <= 180 ms for short prompts (claim summaries ~150–220 tokens).
- Concurrency: steady-state 70–100 rps, burst up to ~300 rps during shift changes.
- Accuracy: entity extraction (policy id, claimant dob, treatment codes) recall >= 95% on seeded prompt set (we'll measure with Redwood Optimize evals).
- Data residency: US-east primary; audit logs stored for 2 years (mentions encryption-at-rest and KMS).
- Logging: redact PHI before any logs leave customer VPC; BRW legal will want a short checklist.

Suggested architecture (POC -> Prod):
1) POC: Private deployment (Redwood Private) in their AWS account (VPC peering/VPN), single region. Use a 3-node Dedicated-like pool (we'll allocate dev GPU sizes) with autoscale off but manual bump to simulate burst. Model: open LLM (quantized) — candidate: Mistral/Redwood-verified 34B quantized to int8 if quality OK. Use Redwood API in private control-plane mode.
2) Prod: Dedicated (reserved capacity) across 2 availability zones, autoscaling policy to handle 95th percentile peaks, prefix caching turned on for common claim templates, prefix/KV caching TTL ~1h for same-claim followups.
3) Fallback: if Private capacity constrained, automatic routing to Redwood-hosted compatible model with response hygiene (PII redaction) — must be allowed by Brasswell (they are sceptical; legal TBD).

Technical requirements / notes from call:
- VPC peering: Brasswell ops will open ports 443 between peered subnets and allow specific IP ranges for control plane. Samir needs our control-plane cidr and certs.
- HSM/KMS: they require HSM-backed key for audit logs and secrets. Need to share Redwood Private KMS integration steps.
- No logs may contain raw SSNs or full card numbers. We should propose on-client redaction layer (pre-send Lambda) as short-term mitigation.
- Model artifact retention: Brasswell wants ability to pin a model version and rollback quickly (they care about deterministic rollouts). Ensure rollout policy in console (canary -> prod) documented in handoff.
- Token-level billing transparency: they want a look at estimated per-claim token cost. We need to produce a back-of-envelope using quantized model + average 200 tokens prompt + 300 tokens completion.

Gotchas / risks identified (working list):
- Latency vs. quant: quantized int8 may reduce memory footprint but could increase tail latency for attention kernels depending on sequence length. Need microbenchmarks on our private infra with their expected sequences.
- Burst handling: their bursts (300 rps) could exceed a small POC pool; need autoscale policy or pre-warm mechanism. Suggest a warm pool for morning shifts.
- Data exfil risk via debug logs: ensure debug-level logging disabled by default in Private.
- Redaction edge cases: OCR'd claims have noisy fields — highlight need for extraction+confidence scoring and human-in-loop workflows for low-confidence outputs.
- HSM onboarding timeline uncertain — could push integration after initial demo. Plan B: use customer-managed KMS (not HSM) for POC.

Prompt engineering notes / safety hooks:
- Use strict instruction templates for extraction tasks. Example template: "Extract policy_number, date_of_loss, claimant_name; if confidence < 0.8 return "HUMAN_REVIEW" for that field."
- Add model-level guardrails: output in strict JSON schema, followed by validator in post-processing. Redwood console should show schema violations.
- Include a short tool-calling concept for deterministic lookups: model returns canonical key + suggestion; downstream service validates policy id against Brasswell DB via a private API call.

Operational items / telemetry we need to expose for them:
- Per-request latency histogram, per-model token counts, cache hit-rate (prefix/KV), and per-route error rates. They also want a daily summary of PHI-redaction events.
- SLA ask: 99.8% avail for dedicated pool (they will push for 99.9 later).

Immediate next steps (owner in parens):
- Send VPC peering spec + control-plane IP list (Ava) — by EOD 11/04.
- Run microbench: 34B-int8 latency + p95 with sample claim prompts (Liam) — by 11/07. Need their sample dataset (anonymized).
- Draft POC runbook (connections, secrets, rollout steps, redaction pattern) (Liam + Priya) — 11/06.
- Temporary redaction Lambda proof-of-concept repo and example (Samir + our infra team) — 11/10.
- Produce cost estimate per-claim with three scenarios: hosted fallback, private small pool, dedicated reserved (Ava) — 11/05.
- Legal: get Brasswell guidance on acceptable fallback (hosted) and log retention policy (Priya / Brasswell legal).

Open questions for Brasswell (to confirm on next call):
- Are we allowed to use hosted fallback for POC demos? If not, we need larger POC footprint.
- Do they need FIPS-140 validated HSM for keys or is customer KMS OK?
- Which fields are considered sensitive beyond SSN/card numbers? (medical notes, diagnosis codes?)
- Acceptable TTL for cached data (they're leaning to 24h? discussed 1h earlier)

Quick decision notes / trade-offs we discussed:
- Model choice: larger model improves extraction accuracy but increases cost and memory. Recommend starting with 34B quantized to test accuracy/cost sweet spot. If extraction recall <95% we try 70B quantized (cost jump) or add a small fine-tuned extractor model ensemble.
- Batching: for latency SLO, keep batch size small (<=4) for live adjuster flows; for background bulk enrichment schedule large batches at off-peak.

Loose TODOs / scribbles:
- Ask data team for 200 anonymized claim samples (mix of OCR & manual typed) + ideal outputs.
- Prepare a short internal demo script highlighting fallback behavior and redaction.
- Add Redwood Optimize eval run for entity extraction (baseline from their dataset).

Notes-to-self: keep doc informal; capture follow-ups after 11/04. Expect legal negotiation on fallback and retention to drive timeline. POC must be low-friction: minimize HSM dependency for first demo.

End of scratchbook.
